page.title: Enhancing Blurry Club Recall
page.description: Applying state-of-the-art segmentation and heuristic blur synthesis to improve difficult blurred-club recall by approximately 30%, with unchanged inference speed.
page.role: My role: I applied a state-of-the-art segmentation model and developed a heuristic augmentation pipeline to improve blurred club head detection.

banner.label: Golf swing pose and club detection

sections.title: Abstract
paragraphs: The previous detector often missed blurred club heads near impact, a critical moment for swing analysis. I applied state-of-the-art segmentation and heuristic blur synthesis to at least double the club head training data after filtering. Difficult blurred-club recall improved by approximately 30%, with no substantial precision loss and unchanged inference speed.

metrics.label: Higher recall on difficult blurred-club cases
Club head training data after filtering

sections.title: Introduction
paragraphs: Rapid club motion, especially in face-on footage and around impact, can blur the club head across multiple pixels. The previous detector handled clearer frames but often missed the club head in these difficult conditions. The target was higher recall across high-quality recordings and videos captured at lower frame rates or in poor lighting.
Blurred-club images made up only about 5% of the available data. Manually selecting these rare frames was inefficient, and collecting more footage would reproduce the same imbalance.

The working hypothesis was that targeted synthetic blur could expand coverage of these failure cases and improve recall without changing the detector architecture. Recall was the primary objective, with a modest precision trade-off considered acceptable.

sections.title: Methods

subsections.title: Isolate the club with an existing model
paragraphs: To augment the moving object selectively, I used a state-of-the-art segmentation model to extract the club from existing frames. This supplied the components for synthesis and let me apply an established model to a task-specific data problem.

subsections.title: Synthesize varied blur with a heuristic method
paragraphs: The extracted components became inputs to a custom heuristic synthesis method. For each original frame, I generated three additional versions with mild, medium, and heavy club blur, increasing exposure to difficult appearances rather than relying on rare real examples alone.

subsections.title: Filter outputs and train the same detector
paragraphs: I filtered out low-quality synthetic results before using the augmented data for training. The retained club head training data was at least twice the original size. Keeping the detector architecture unchanged made training-data coverage the main intervention and preserved inference speed.

sections.note: Proprietary synthesis heuristics, filtering rules, and training settings are omitted; the description focuses on the problem each implementation step addresses.

sections.title: Results
paragraphs: Difficult blurred-club recall improved by approximately 30% over the previous model, with no substantial observed precision decrease. The detector architecture and inference speed remained unchanged.
sections.note: Yellow shows the previous predictions; green shows the updated predictions.

subsections.title: What the improvement means
paragraphs: Compared with the previous detector, the updated model recovered more difficult blurred-club cases after targeted dataset augmentation. The result supports segmentation-guided synthesis as a practical way to address underrepresented failure modes using an existing model and task-specific heuristics.
No overfitting was observed. Together with the preserved precision, this suggests that the generated examples captured useful cues from real blur, rather than only synthetic artifacts.

subsections.title: A repeatable augmentation stage for MLOps
paragraphs: The implemented synthesis and filtering pipeline turns existing footage into additional training examples with controlled blur severity. This gives model iteration a repeatable data-preparation stage while retaining the same inference architecture.

For CI/CD integration, versioned source data and synthesis settings could be paired with automated data checks and evaluation gates for difficult-case recall, precision, and inference speed. This would help the team validate augmentation changes before promoting a model.

subsections.title: Next iteration: reconstruct the background
paragraphs: An inpainting model could fill the region where the original club was segmented out, producing a cleaner background for synthesis. This could reduce compositing artifacts and make the generated blur more realistic. A subsequent evaluation should check whether that added realism improves difficult-case recall while preserving precision.

sections.title: Conclusion
paragraphs: By applying state-of-the-art segmentation and designing a heuristic augmentation pipeline, I improved difficult blurred-club recall by approximately 30% with no substantial precision loss or change in inference speed. The project demonstrates hands-on model integration and targeted data engineering.
